Historical July maxima average ~25°C, so current guidance reflects slightly above-average but not extreme conditions.

Official guidance from the China Meteorological Administration and global models (ECMWF, GFS) currently converge on a warm, mostly cloudy day with daytime maxima near 28–31 °C, tempered by Yellow Sea breezes that limit inland-style heating. Traders are therefore pricing the narrow band of uncertainty between a typical maritime-cooling scenario and a modestly warmer, less cloudy solution, with the next model runs and any updated CMA briefing likely to narrow the distribution before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus clusters tightly around 30–32°C for Manila’s July 24 high, reflecting substantial short-range forecast uncertainty driven by the southwest monsoon. Variable cloud cover, rainfall timing, and southwesterly flow strength—key controls on surface heating and evaporative cooling—produce divergent model outputs for solar insolation and boundary-layer moisture. PAGASA climatology places late-July means near 31°C, yet daily deviations hinge on monsoon trough position and any passing tropical disturbances. Updated global and regional model runs expected over the next 48 hours will likely narrow the distribution as observational data constrain precipitation and wind forecasts.
